assertions.contract_summary: The workflow's only trigger is `pull_request` restricted to the `main` branch.
assertions.rationale: The durable contract (trigger is pull_request, branches restricted to main) is structural, but the raw regex locks four consecutive lines together with their exact block-style indentation and a block-sequence item (`      - main`). Empirically verified on the live workflow with temporary meaning-preserving mutations: rewriting the sequence in the equally valid and widely used flow style `branches: [main]` breaks it, restyling the block to 4-space nesting breaks it, and spelling out the default `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` breaks it -- none of which change what the workflow does. Unlike the single-line `^\s+key: value$` checks in this class, this one pins a multi-line serialization rather than a value, the raw form is brittle to presentation-only edits, so it should become a parsed-YAML structural check (`data['on']['pull_request']['branches'] == ['main']`); not converted in this PR.

The literal contains no whitespace, indentation or prose, so no reformatting of the workflow can break it. Category B.

assertions.contract_summary: The workflow declares neither a `schedule:` nor a `workflow_dispatch:` trigger.
assertions.rationale: A structural per-line-prefix negative regex with leading `^\s*`, so it is indentation-agnostic and matches on YAML key structure rather than on any prose. It keeps PR CI free of the production workflow's scheduled and manually dispatched triggers. Matches this suite's established `structural regex, not a raw substring` B precedent.

assertions.contract_summary: The workflow declares top-level `permissions:` with `contents: read`.
assertions.rationale: The permission value itself is a fixed field/value from Actions' closed vocabulary, but the raw regex additionally locks `permissions:` and its child onto two exactly adjacent lines at exactly 2-space indentation. Empirically verified with temporary meaning-preserving mutations of the live workflow: inserting an explanatory comment line between the key and its child (`permissions:` / `  # read-only: CI never writes to the repository` / `  contents: read`) breaks it, and restyling the block to 4-space nesting breaks it, while neither changes the granted permissions. The same tranche's single-line field checks survive both. The value is structural but its two-line raw form is brittle, so it should become a parsed-YAML check on the top-level permissions mapping; not converted in this PR.

assertions.contract_summary: The workflow never grants `contents: write` anywhere.
assertions.rationale: A negative check on a structural permission field/value token drawn from Actions' closed read/write/none vocabulary. It is the load-bearing half of the read-only contract: it also covers job-level permission blocks that a top-level-only check would miss. Empirically verified: flipping the live workflow to `contents: write` fails this method. Category B (`permission field/value`).

assertions.contract_summary: The checkout step pins `actions/checkout` to the full commit SHA `3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1`, documented as v7.0.1.

Empirically verified with temporary meaning-preserving mutations: rewording the comment to `# pinned to v7.0.1`, dropping the comment, or widening the space before `#` each breaks this assertion although the workflow runs identically (appending after the comment does not, since it is a substring check -- confirming the brittleness is in the comment's exact rendering). Per the established rule this is not `B just because it contains a structural element`: it should be split into a structural check on `uses: actions/checkout@<sha>` plus a separate version-comment check; not converted in this PR. It is not D -- a currently pinned action SHA is the current workflow structural contract, not historical acceptance evidence.

assertions.contract_summary: Every `actions/checkout` ref in both workflows is exactly 40 characters long, i.e. a full commit SHA rather than an abbreviated one.

This is the same `$`-anchored single-line key/value shape that the accepted tranche 3k classification records as Category B four times (`fetch-depth: 0`, `persist-credentials: false`, `timeout-minutes: 15`, `cancel-in-progress: true`). assertions.rationale: A count over `(?m)^\s*-\s*package-ecosystem:` block-sequence item markers, i.e. a check on YAML list structure rather than on any prose or fixed layout. The leading `^\s*` and the `\s*` after the dash make it indentation- and spacing-agnostic. assertions.contract_summary: The Dependabot update entry sets `package-ecosystem` to `github-actions`, matched at the key on an active mapping line (block-scalar content excluded) and accepting YAML's equivalent scalar renderings (double-quoted, single-quoted, plain).
assertions.rationale: BL-038 tranche 4c (R4-A atomic structural extraction). The Category C reason was `quote-style lock` and nothing else: the durable contract is the atomic value `package-ecosystem` = `github-actions`, but the raw regex additionally required DOUBLE QUOTES, so the empirically equivalent renderings `package-ecosystem: 'github-actions'` and `package-ecosystem: github-actions` broke the assertion while Dependabot behaved identically. The regex now anchors to the key at line level and accepts the three equivalent scalar renderings of the same value; a real value change still fails. The assertion scopes its own haystack before matching: the file is reduced to its active mapping lines, because block-scalar content (a `key: |` or `key: >` header and every following line indented deeper than it) is plain text rather than fields of this document. The expected literal must therefore occur as an active line. Measured non-active forms that do NOT satisfy it: a commented-out line, and the same text placed inside a block scalar -- verified for the `|`, `|-`, `|+`, `|2`, `|2-`, `|-2`, `>` and `>-` indicators, for an indicator followed by a trailing comment, for a block nested under `schedule`, for a block whose content itself contains a header-looking line, for blank lines inside the content, and for a block placed before the real fields. Only relative depth is used, so indentation width stays outside the contract. What this assertion does NOT decide on its own is position on the active path: it is a narrow line-anchored key/value match over active lines, not a YAML parser. The full structural path (updates -> the direct update entry -> its direct `package-ecosystem` / `directory` / `schedule` -> that schedule's direct `interval`) is a complementary guarantee held by the tranche 4c-prep guard, which no longer requires any quote style. One assertion in, one assertion out: id, ordinal, targets and assertion_api unchanged. Trailing YAML comments are tolerated only with valid token separation: a `#` attached directly to a plain scalar stays part of that scalar, so `value#suffix` is a different value and does not satisfy the expected atomic value.

assertions.contract_summary: No other package ecosystem (`pip`, `npm`, `docker`, `npm-workspaces`) is configured.

The literals are quoted ecosystem tokens rather than ordinary prose words, so unlike the optional-policy-field guard in this class they cannot plausibly collide with explanatory text, and no meaning-preserving reformatting of the live file makes this assertion FAIL -- which is the operative Category C test in this corpus. (Measured limitation recorded deliberately: because the literals embed the double quotes, restyling the file to plain scalars would leave this guard passing but vacuous rather than failing; that is a robustness gap in the guard, not the meaning-preserving-breakage that defines Category C.) Category B (`prohibited ecosystem identifier`).
